course.title: Southeast Asia Through Time
course.description: Investigate how people in Southeast Asia lived, connected across seas, faced changing power, built new nations, and preserve their histories. Explore real objects, archives, places, photographs, and different points of view.

sections.title: Evidence and early connections
sections.question: What do objects and places tell us about early lives and trade by sea?
sections.description: Study a pot from Ban Chiang, old boat planks from Butuan and maps of Melaka, and learn to tell what a source shows from what we guess.

sections.title: Trade, power and everyday lives
sections.question: Who gained, who worked, and who challenged unfair rules?
sections.description: Follow nutmeg from Banda, rubber from Malaya and letters from Kartini, and ask whose story each source tells.

sections.title: War, independence and rebuilding
sections.question: How did war and independence change different communities?
sections.description: See how war changed daily life in Singapore, compare how Indonesia and Malaya became independent, and look at how Timor-Leste rebuilt its schools.

sections.title: People, memory and shared histories
sections.question: How do people choose which stories to keep and share?
sections.description: Visit the port of Hội An and the temple of Borobudur, then plan a small exhibition that tells a shared history fairly.
